title: Gate Copilot issue automation behind readiness checks
body:
Premature Copilot assignment was launching on newly opened issues that were still in `❓ status:needs-info`, which led to placeholder-only runs and recurring empty PRs. This change introduces a readiness gate that computes label state from issue-form content before Copilot can be assigned.

- **Readiness workflow**
  - Adds `.github/workflows/copilot-readiness-check.yml` to evaluate issues on `opened`, `edited`, `reopened`, `labeled`, and `unlabeled`.
  - Serializes runs per issue with workflow concurrency to avoid label races from self-triggered label updates.

- **Shared readiness rules**
  - Adds `.github/scripts/issue-readiness-check.js` as the single source of truth for issue readiness.
  - Validates supported MEMELAND issue templates by checking:
    - required fields are present
    - placeholder/template text has been replaced
    - rights confirmations are checked
    - multilingual update requests contain real text for each selected language
    - media requests include an actual asset source, not just placement notes

- **Label state management**
  - Automatically adds `🤖 ready-for-copilot` when an issue is complete.
  - Removes `🤖 ready-for-copilot` and keeps/adds `❓ status:needs-info` when the issue is incomplete.
  - Treats `⏸️ no-agent` as a hard opt-out and suppresses readiness-label updates.

- **Assignment hardening**
  - Keeps `.github/workflows/copilot-assign.yml` as the final launcher.
  - Changes assignment to explicit ready-label gating.
  - Re-fetches current issue labels before assigning Copilot so stale `labeled` event payloads cannot launch the agent in an intermediate state.

- **Key flow**
  ```yaml
  on:
    issues:
      types: [labeled]

  if: >
    github.event.label.name == '🤖 ready-for-copilot' &&
    !contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, '⏸️ no-agent') &&
    !contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, '❓ status:needs-info')
  ```

This moves the system from “assign first, fail later” to “validate first, then assign,” which should eliminate the common empty-PR path while keeping the opt-out and safety rails intact.
